Implemented persistent operator-controlled stimulus lifetime, active randomization, right A/B shortcuts, either-stick preset cycling, and clamped viewer-distance control; focused/full JVM, static, native, shader, and APK build checks passed, and the Q-ending serial-scoped attended run launched with exact pre-run property restoration evidence preserved.

Unified panel, controller-cycle, and right-A randomization selection authority; reduced the interference shader to one signal evaluation with derivative band limiting and per-pixel decorrelated noise; requested Spatial SDK boost performance only while output is selected; focused and full JVM, shader/APK build, workflow/static, and focused native checks passed; launched the inert warning-first attended build with exact property isolation and zero bounded launch fatals.

Diffed the exact pinned Trevor source and restored interference randomization bounds, rounding, and sparse branches plus temporal control limits; replaced dropout-sensitive A handling with valid-sample release latches; added shared right-trigger/panel app-private Store and stored-list Load with exact profile and distance persistence; the full JVM suite, post-change focused JVM suite, 45 focused native tests, all app static gates, shader packaging, and APK assembly passed; launched the inert warning-first Q-ending attended run with exact prelaunch property isolation and no carrier before user selection.

Changed VR Strobe right-controller sample validity from Meta's transient active flag to stable right-controller identity while retaining valid-sample release latches; added a single-draw 64-segment cylindrical circular-arc carrier bent by a vertex uniform, active-panel flat/curved control, curved-mode left-Y concavity and right-Y distance authorities, and stored-profile codec v2 with v1 migration. Focused and full JVM suites, all app static gates, 45 focused native tests, Spatial shader compilation, and dedicated APK assembly passed. Serial-scoped install-r preserved all three existing profiles; the warning-first launch had zero bounded fatals, and live controller evidence recorded 22 successful rapid A randomizations across preset revisions with no randomize failure. Curvature appearance and concavity direction remain attended headset checks.

Replaced the outside-facing horizontal cylinder with one radial 16-ring by 48-segment disc that bends in both axes from a flat circle to a viewer-facing hemisphere through a bounded vertex uniform. Randomize now configures a hidden standby material and atomically publishes it by swapping the existing scene object's mesh, preserving one visible draw and explicit renderer-publication markers. Focused and full JVM suites, all Spatial Camera Panel static gates, 45 focused native tests, all 52 Spatial shader variants, and dedicated APK assembly passed. Serial-scoped install-r and cold launch on the Q-ending USB target preserved four stored profiles; only the strobe feature was enabled, the warning remained first, output remained inactive, and the bounded launch window had no fatal.

Made new VR Strobe sessions default to curved mode at maximum concavity, the full 180-degree viewer-facing hemisphere, while keeping version-1 stored-profile migration explicitly flat. Moved the exclusive Strobe safety UI to a Spatial SDK compositor layer at z-index 100 above the always-depth-visible stimulus, recentered and reoriented the panel from the current viewer pose on every B-open, and excluded right A from Compose panel-click input so its only action is one lifecycle-preserving global randomize. All 93 JVM tests, all Spatial Camera Panel static gates, 45 focused native tests, dedicated shader/APK assembly, and serial-scoped install-r passed. The cold Q-ending launch reported the warning first, output inactive, panel layer ready at z-index 100, A panel input disabled, live viewer pose, seven preserved stored profiles, and no bounded fatal.

Corrected event 43's host-marker-only panel foreground and A-isolation assumptions after attended feedback showed that A still activated Pause/Resume and the panel still composed behind the stimulus. The Strobe panel now explicitly uses OPAQUE rather than the Spatial SDK Layer default MASKED blend so its z-index-100 compositor surface does not depend on the depth-hole path defeated by the stimulus DepthTest.ALWAYS/no-depth-write material. The Compose root consumes controller A before focused controls, blocks descendant focus, and clears/disables its backing view while the ECS entity is hidden; global controller A remains the sole randomize authority. Focused and full JVM suites, all Spatial Camera Panel static gates, 45 focused native tests, shader/native APK assembly, and serial-scoped install-r passed. APK SHA-256 2c5f15c66e62c3f29d232dd5ba3b02d93b551f324de309e9f33f267763d89b6d cold-launched on the Q-ending Quest 3S with warning first, output inactive, explicit opaque panel layer at z-index 100, preview-key policy active, seven stored profiles preserved, and no startup fatal. Panel foreground and controller behavior await attended headset confirmation.

Corrected event 44 after attended feedback showed explicit OPAQUE layer composition and Compose key interception were still insufficient: the panel remained behind the stimulus and A could still activate Pause/Resume with the ECS panel hidden. Reused the repository's prior attended full-field projection A/B instead of making another layer-order assumption: the Strobe panel is now physically foregrounded at 0.22 m, nearer than the carrier's 0.35 m minimum, and scaled by 0.22/0.82 to retain its accepted apparent size. The stimulus changed from ALWAYS/no-write to LESS_OR_EQUAL depth testing with depth writes enabled. The active UI and action bindings no longer contain any Pause/Resume route, and B-close additionally hides the native PanelSceneObject as well as clearing/disabling the Compose root and hiding the ECS entity. The full JVM suite, all Spatial Camera Panel static/workflow gates, 45 focused native tests, and dedicated shader/native APK assembly passed. APK SHA-256 81f4e4a0019ef46ba6b9fe0828ffe36ab4fe875d40989743f85105c9db823976 cold-launched on the Q-ending Quest 3S with warning first, output inactive, physical-foreground/depth contract reported, seven stored profiles preserved, and no startup fatal. Runtime markers explicitly retain attended foreground proof as pending.

Corrected event 45 after attended feedback rejected the 0.22 m physical-foreground experiment: the panel was uncomfortably close and no longer accepted trigger clicks, although grab and B-toggle still worked. Restored the comfortable, previously trigger-tested 0.82 m unscaled panel pose. Foreground authority now suppresses both the stimulus carrier's native SceneObject and ECS entity while the panel is visible without changing warning, profile selection, elapsed output, or safety lifecycle; closing the panel restores the carrier. Every accepted preset, designer, or stored-profile Begin auto-closes the panel so the stimulus becomes visible after the 500 ms black lead-in. The no-Pause/Resume UI contract remains intact. Full JVM tests and shader compilation, all Spatial Camera Panel workflow/static gates, 45 focused native tests, and dedicated native APK assembly passed. APK SHA-256 4b890522964c2330f8d93fdc1ba53af56c67e9ce1e9e36f44a11bd5639157145 installed in place and cold-launched on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, panel at 0.82 m, carrier-guard mode reported, output inactive, seven saved profiles preserved, and no startup fatal. Trigger interaction, accepted-Begin auto-close, carrier suppression/restoration, and panel comfort await attended confirmation.

Corrected the repeated right-A reliability assumptions retained through events 40-46 after attended feedback still observed apparent pause/unpause versus randomize. The exact stack audit found two action-capable ingress families and an unproved standby SceneObject mesh assignment: Kotlin could swap its active material reference even when the visible mesh did not publish, leaving per-frame time updates on the invisible material and making the visible stimulus appear paused. Right A now dispatches only from one confirmed Spatial SDK right-controller snapshot edge; Android key/motion copies are consumed as non-dispatching secondary ingress. Every press has numbered dispatch/completion markers linked to randomize-start, renderer-publication, and randomize-complete markers. The latent PAUSED state and pause/resume methods were removed. Randomize updates the single material already bound to the visible carrier, increments a renderer revision, and performs no SceneObject mesh swap while retaining one visible draw. The accepted comfortable 0.82 m carrier-suppressed panel setup is unchanged. All 96 JVM tests, all Spatial Camera Panel workflow/static gates, 45 focused native tests, shader packaging, and dedicated APK assembly passed. APK SHA-256 ff2287aed1498d1318f1ea0b666050ffe3372c8f1628f859e3f722527194e2b5 installed in place and cold-launched on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, output inactive, eight saved profiles preserved, and no bounded startup fatal; attended repeated-A proof remains pending.

Corrected event 47's remaining profile-viability and foreground assumptions after attended feedback confirmed that A no longer paused output but extreme random profiles still appeared unreliable and too often collapsed to flat color. Live bounded runtime evidence showed sustained frame-drop pressure, about 57/90 FPS and near-saturated GPU utilization. The pinned browser audit showed that raw editor bounds were not a Quest viability contract: independently defaulted vignette center/edge produce equal smoothstep edges in most random runs, while bright-only palettes combined with -1..1 brightness and 0..3 contrast commonly clip to flat output. Randomize now uses quest-reliable-v1 inside Trevor's outer bounds: separated palettes, bounded brightness/contrast, valid or disabled vignettes, at most three active patterns with one optional distortion and wave branch, and 1..30 Hz/20..80 percent temporal values. The shader rejects equal-edge vignette input, and candidate markers report envelope acceptance, branch counts, and transaction duration. The comfortable 0.82 m panel is retained; carrier default distance/radius both double from 0.62/1.42 m to 1.24/2.84 m with a 1.05 m minimum, preserving angular coverage while keeping the selected carrier active behind the opaque panel. Stored-profile codec v3 migrates v1/v2 distances once and retains the v1 flat-shape migration. All 98 JVM tests, all Spatial Camera Panel workflow/static gates, 45 focused native tests, all 52 Spatial shader variants, and dedicated APK assembly passed. APK SHA-256 0cf80300512589c5fb8ffbb8e8c716dc56542d184003132bff17d688135293d4 installed in place and cold-launched on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, depth-separated foreground markers, eight saved profiles preserved, and no bounded startup fatal. Attended random profile viability, panel occlusion over active output, angular coverage, and GPU-frame improvement remain pending.

Corrected events 47-48 after attended feedback showed that right A remained unreliable while right B and thumbstick flicks from the same tracked controller were consistently accepted, ruling out a general controller or performance failure. The exact app stack retained Android key/motion edges for B and flick but deliberately discarded them for A, making A alone depend on a separate Spatial snapshot edge. One app-owned A action arbiter now accepts the first Android key/motion or Spatial snapshot observation and suppresses duplicate platform observations within 120 ms; numbered ingress, action, renderer-publication, and completion receipts remain linked and no Pause/Resume route exists. Corrected event 48's overly coarse random envelope after attended feedback confirmed flat/extreme cases were resolved but structural resolution was too restricted. Quest randomization now uses quest-reliable-v2: the palette, brightness, vignette, active-pattern, distortion, and wave guards remain unchanged, while a mixed coarse/fine band permits global scale 7.5, stripe/ripple period 36, ray count 40, and Perlin scale 22 without adding fragment evaluations. Tests explicitly prove repeated Android-only A presses, Spatial fallback, cross-route single-action deduplication, coarse results, and fine-detail results. All 103 JVM tests, all Spatial Camera Panel workflow/static gates, 45 focused native tests, shader packaging, and dedicated APK assembly passed. APK SHA-256 d6cbbb2c790c26d06a3fa445eb96b234cb70bd968f851ad2cf3e153bca98345e installed in place and cold-launched on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, intended package focus, eight saved profiles preserved, and no startup fatal. Attended repeated-A reliability and coarse/fine balance remain pending.

Corrected event 49's remaining input and renderer-publication assumptions after attended feedback said A began reliably but appeared progressively less effective. Durable app-private evidence from that exact run contained 145 physical right-A rising edges, 145 action dispatches, 145 completed randomize transactions, zero duplicate suppressions, and 1-12 ms host transaction duration, proving that the perceived losses were downstream of controller ingress. The active-material path cleared 175 profile attributes and then rewrote all 160 declared pattern-slot vectors plus globals on every press, producing roughly 347 asynchronous Spatial material mutations while its renderer-published marker proved only host submission. Randomize now writes only active pattern payloads, commits their authoritative counts last, never clears or rewrites inactive trailing slots, and submits 9 attributes for temporal profiles or at most 27 for the guarded three-pattern interference profile. Runtime receipts now distinguish update-submitted from a later scene-frame boundary and retain attended visibility as the adoption proof. Quest randomization uses quest-reliable-v3: unchanged palette, brightness, vignette, three-pattern, distortion, wave, and temporal guards combine with 60-percent fine-band selection and outer-compatible maxima of global scale 16, stripe/ripple and ray period 50, and Perlin scale 40 without adding fragment evaluations. All 105 JVM tests, all Spatial Camera Panel workflow/static gates, 45 focused native tests, shader packaging, dedicated APK assembly, and manifest identity verification passed. Dedicated APK SHA-256 9c9f70501838dacfa7a2e192dd77ae2092727eedf3eeb42546456abaacc54da1 installed in place and cold-launched under the intended VR Strobe test package on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, output inactive, eight saved profiles preserved, and zero bounded startup fatals. Attended repeated-A visible-adoption reliability and coarse/fine balance remain pending.

All 109 JVM tests, four browser contract tests, 45 focused native tests, VR Strobe, panel-facing, app, and workflow static gates, 52 packaged shader variants, native receipt build, dedicated APK assembly, and manifest identity verification passed. Attended confirmation of 4.00 m initial placement, left-X Store, trigger panel clicks, and headset appearance remains pending.

Corrected event 51's generic browser-editor presentation after comparison with Trevor Hewitt's pinned portal and deployed designer surfaces. The browser now seeds Trevor's complete ordered source list—five simulations and four temporal strobes—using the same stable Quest catalog IDs and the exact interference payloads from pinned commit 52c71cc069f4102bc4148e05c5fd3fc4d5466479. Its landing page reproduces the original two-column Stimulus Selection cards and design-page landmarks; simulation editing uses the familiar full-canvas view with a 400 px right Interference Shader rail, source group names, sliders plus numeric readbacks, and pattern families, while temporal editing uses the compact upper-left collapsed STROBE/CONTROLS panel. Additive Quest profile transfer, naming, distance, curved-mode, and concavity controls retain the version-1 JSON authority. Existing browser storage gains missing originals, preserves edited/user profiles, and removes only the untouched old starter; explicit Restore original set resets the nine pinned entries while preserving additions. Seven browser contract/catalog tests and the focused VR Strobe static gate passed. Browser inspection confirmed nine default exportable profiles, source-faithful portal, warning-gated live simulation and temporal designers, correct 4.00 m readback, no horizontal desktop overflow, and no browser diagnostics. No headset, APK, ADB, or runtime state was changed.

Replaced event 52's per-designer preview warning with a dedicated browser entry page whose acknowledgement persists only for the current browser session and remains independent of the Quest safety flow. Selecting a stimulus after acknowledgement begins the flat preview immediately. One document-level command layer, suppressed for editable controls and repeated keydown events, now owns Left/Right current-set cycling, Space pause/resume, Up quest-reliable-v3 randomization, Down exact per-profile LIFO restore, and S session-only snapshot storage. Randomization history is bounded to 128 independent cloned entries per profile and is invalidated by manual edits; session snapshots join profile selection and explicit bundle download without entering persistent local browser storage, and disappear on reload. Ten browser contract/catalog/session tests, the focused VR Strobe static gate, and the Spatial Camera Panel workflow static gate passed. Live browser validation on a fresh origin confirmed warning-first entry, no repeat warning after accept plus reload, active preview on selection, profile cycling, pause/resume, changed random output, exact restore, session-save creation and wraparound selection, session-save removal on reload, and zero browser errors. No headset, APK, ADB, or Quest runtime state was changed.

Corrected event 50's remaining assumption that completed one-shot active-material writes would necessarily become visibly distinct. Durable app-private evidence from the attended run contained 84 right-A dispatches, 84 distinct accepted candidates, 84 renderer submissions, 84 later-frame observations, and 84 completed transactions with zero suppression or transaction failure, ruling out controller ingress and the unified selection authority. Bounded inspection of Meta Spatial SDK 0.13.1 confirmed that SceneMaterial exposes only individual native setAttribute calls and no batch or atomic material-update API. Randomize still preserves the single live carrier, no-pause lifecycle, no mesh swap, one draw, and at most 27 profile writes, but now increments the renderer revision before output publication and continuously carries a deterministic phase offset plus alternating palette polarity through modeTime.zw on every scene tick. The fragment shader uses this cheap generation signature for interference spatial/palette phase and temporal phase/color ordering, so an accepted revision retains a GPU-visible distinction even when one-shot profile uniforms are adopted late. Focused controller, randomization, and GPU-plan JVM tests passed, including 10,000 adjacent revision transitions; the VR Strobe and panel-facing static gates passed; the modified shader compiled into the 52-variant package; and the dedicated APK assembled with matching manifest/package identity. APK SHA-256 0f39604e1db66b24ae14bd09b99674f8ae43f588cd0511efbd772c9a7c761262 installed in place and cold-launched under the intended VR Strobe package on the selected Quest 3S, with warning first, output inactive, stored-profile count zero, and no bounded startup fatal. Attended repeated-A visible-adoption reliability remains pending.

Corrected event 54 after attended feedback precisely distinguished its continuously reasserted generation phase from meaningful randomized parameter adoption: every A press changed the instantaneous phase, but only every few presses visibly adopted the candidate profile. Durable evidence from that run contained 60 dispatches, 60 strongly varying accepted candidates, 60 one-shot submissions, 60 later-frame observations, and zero suppression or failure, confirming stale one-shot profile uniforms rather than input or random-domain failure. Randomize now queues every accepted profile, addresses active material attributes through cached numeric indices, publishes no more than six profile uniforms per scene tick, repeats the complete bounded pass once, commits active pattern counts last in each pass, and advances the continuously reasserted visible generation only after the profile publication completes. An interference candidate uses 26 profile attributes across ten scene ticks and 52 total writes, below the 175-write initial clear and former 347-write per-action path; temporal uses eight attributes across four ticks. The single live material, one draw, no-mesh-swap lifecycle, no-pause contract, and one interference signal evaluation per fragment remain unchanged. The full Android unit suite and revised VR Strobe static gate passed, the shader compiled into all 52 packaged variants, and the dedicated APK assembled with exact manifest/package/hash agreement. APK SHA-256 c53ce012e89f0dc02868400ea68101dcb819b7e2f5d7cd0369f09eb6735991c5 installed in place and cold-launched under the intended VR Strobe package on the selected Quest 3S with warning first, output inactive, live process, and zero bounded startup fatals. Attended repeated-A meaningful-profile adoption remains pending.

Added the requested experimental depth deformation as an opt-in interference-only vertex path. The UI defaults off and exposes a sanitized symmetric 0..5 cm maximum, with a 2.5 cm initial tuning value; temporal presets explicitly remain undeformed. A cheap band-limited procedural witness maps palette luminance from negative displacement at black through zero at mid-gray to positive displacement at white, then offsets the carrier along an analytic viewer-facing flat or spherical normal. Carrier tessellation increases from 16-by-48 to 32-by-96 (3073 vertices, 6048 triangles) while retaining one material, one visible draw, the single interference fragment evaluation, no gl_FragDepth, and no geometry rebuild during tuning. All 70 focused Strobe tests, all 115 app JVM tests, the focused static gate, native receipt build, all 52 packaged Spatial shader variants, APK assembly, manifest identity verification, serial-scoped install, and cold-launch passed. APK SHA-256 f597f9a9ab111960b852134204253a5c3eac0a6ec3a50d80dff98c3181edc199 launched on the selected Quest 3S with the prior Strobe property preserved, warning first, output inactive, a live advancing frame loop, and zero bounded startup fatals. Attended toggle, amplitude, parallax, silhouette, comfort, and GPU-frame comparison remain pending.

Corrected event 56 after attended feedback identified that a button labeled ON did not clearly distinguish current state from the action available on press and that the 5 cm tuning ceiling was insufficient. The active panel now displays current/effective state independently and labels the button TURN DEPTH DEFORMATION ON or OFF according to its next action; temporal output reports effective OFF while retaining the saved interference preference. The sanitized symmetric maximum now reaches 1.42 m, exactly half the 2.84 m carrier radius, while retaining a 2.5 cm default and millimeter quantization. A quadratic slider mapping preserves fine low-range control despite the expanded 0..1.42 m envelope, and the panel labels values above 20 cm as an experimental self-occlusion, faceting, and comfort stress range. All 71 focused Strobe tests, all 116 app JVM tests, the focused static gate, native receipt build, packaged Spatial shader set, APK assembly, manifest identity verification, serial-scoped replacement install, and cold-launch passed. APK SHA-256 eb259e40ab769a43c8278090ebfa278427f11779b39a2e6a18724a51d06cb30a launched on the selected Quest 3S with the prior Strobe property preserved, warning first, output inactive, a live 2000-frame startup witness, and zero bounded startup fatals. Attended state-label clarity and expanded-range visual, comfort, and performance comparison remain pending.

Corrected event 57 after attended feedback accepted the expanded depth effect, requested default-on maximum displacement, and reported renewed GPU redlining. Read-only compositor evidence from that run showed the app already at GPU level 4 with GPU utilization about 0.84..0.85 versus CPU utilization about 0.17..0.20, confirming overdraw/shader pressure rather than an available higher performance level. Interference depth now defaults enabled at the full symmetric 1.42 m range. Geometry follows the interference palette coordinate instead of post-palette luminance: two-color slot 1 is far and slot 2 near; three-color slot 1 is far, slot 2 neutral, and slot 3 near, with polarity reversing color and depth together. RGB palette reconstruction, post processing, and luma dot work were removed from the vertex shader. Fine fragment detail remains unchanged, while depth-only spatial bandwidth eases from 12 above 5 cm to 4 at maximum displacement to limit steep folds. The carrier's tested +Z viewer-facing winding now uses FRONT_SIDED material culling instead of DOUBLE_SIDED so backwards folds are rejected before fragment shading. All 118 app JVM tests, the focused VR Strobe static gate, JSON and whitespace checks, native receipt build, 52 Spatial shader variants, APK assembly, and manifest/hash verification passed. APK SHA-256 97d608b8717058589b574fb2f7b09275749e5c7ad0b07e581398b30b15e38e0c replaced only the intended test package and cold-launched on the Q-ending Quest with the prior true enable property preserved, warning first, a live 1000-frame witness, and zero bounded startup fatals. Attended confirmation of front-face visibility, default-on maximum palette-relative depth, fold quality, and comparative GPU utilization remains pending.

No headset, ADB, APK install, source deletion, reset, stash, checkout, commit, or push occurred.

New Morphovision work resumes only from Rusty-Symmetric-Morphovision/morphospace; new Strobe work resumes only from apps/spatial-vr-strobe-android/morphospace.
